title: High-Throughput gDNA Extraction of Mosquito Tissues using QIAcube HT
author: Jack Dorman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhgcj3sw
materials: Follow software and manual for cleanup instructions.

steps.title: Separate mosquito body parts
steps.instruction: Using clean tweezers, separate the head and abdomen from the thorax on a sterile petri dish. Transfer the body segment that will be used for extraction (either thorax or abdomen) into a 2 mL RB tube containing a 5 mm stainless‑steel bead. Place the remaining two segments in the other two RB tubes and store all tubes at –20 °C or –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare water bath and Buffer ATL
steps.instruction: Set a water bath to 56 °C. Inspect Buffer ATL for visible precipitates; if any are present, incubate Buffer ATL at 56 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Make Lysis Buffer working solution
steps.instruction: In a 15–50 mL Falcon tube (size chosen based on the number of samples), prepare Lysis Buffer by mixing 180 µL Buffer ATL with 1.3 µL Reagent DX per mosquito sample. Vortex the mixture at 2000 rpm for at least 15 seconds. Add an extra 10 % volume to compensate for buffer loss.

steps.title: Add Lysis Buffer to sample tubes
steps.instruction: Using an Eppendorf Repeater, dispense 180 µL of the well‑vortexed Lysis Buffer into each RB tube that already contains the steel bead and the selected body segment.

steps.title: Mechanical lysis in TissueLyser
steps.instruction: Visually balance the tubes in a TissueLyser adapter and load into the TissueLyser II. Then:

substeps.instruction: Lyse abdomen samples at 30 Hz for 30 seconds.
Lyse thorax samples at 30 Hz for 1 minute 40 seconds.
Spin the tubes for 30 seconds at 15,000 rpm.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K to each tube. Vortex at 2000 rpm for 10 seconds, then spin down for 30 seconds at 15,000 rpm.

steps.title: Incubate samples at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in floating racks and immerse in the 56 °C water bath. Incubate for 1 hour.

steps.title: Spin down after incubation
steps.instruction: After incubation, spin the tubes for 30 seconds at 15,000 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare QIAcube reagents and run
steps.instruction: While samples incubate, start the QIAcube instrument, select the “DNeasy InsectLysates200ul AL‑EtoH_tv” file, and use the default parameters (software version 1.6.61). Then:

substeps.instruction: Check Buffer AL for precipitate; if present, incubate at 56 °C for ~5 minutes.
Dispense the QIAcube‑provided buffer volumes into reagent troughs under a biosafety hood.
Add an extra 10 % of AL/Ethanol to account for transfer loss.
Mix the AL/Ethanol solution in a 50 mL Falcon tube by inverting at least five times (or until homogeneous).
If running fewer than 96 samples, hermetically seal unused columns/wells with a Tape Pad.
Ensure the Elution plate, QIAamp plate, and the S‑Block are positioned firmly in the upper‑left portion of their carriages.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to S‑Block
steps.instruction: Move the tubes to a magnetic rack to immobilize the 5 mm beads. Using a 200 µL pipette, immediately transfer as much of the 200 µL supernatant as possible into the S‑Block (expect occasional loss of 5–10 µL).

steps.title: Load S‑Block onto QIAcube
steps.instruction: Place the properly labelled S‑Block onto the QIAcube carriage (labels should contain date, sample type, project name, etc.). Follow the QIAcube software and manual to start the DNA extraction run and save the Pre‑Run report.

steps.title: Finalize run and store DNA
steps.instruction: When the run finishes, save the Post‑Run report and transfer the labelled Elution Plate (containing extracted DNA) to storage at –20 °C for short‑term or –80 °C for long‑term storage, unless immediate quality assessment is performed.
